failed_predictions: at least 8 of 16 seeds show a deeper proportional rooted-membership gap after intervention removal

interpretation: Temporary underground disruption robustly reduces the rooted armed-membership stock on average through day 360, but does not robustly reduce already-fielded force over the same horizon.
The development claim of a reliable lagged fielded-force decline did not replicate and is dropped.
The fresh replication instead reveals a stock-pressure divergence: lower rooted membership coexists with higher recruitment hazard and stronger footholds after disruption is removed.
This motivates a direct test of whether reducing armed membership expands recruitment eligibility faster than it removes access to recruitment channels.
